turns.content: Hey! So I'm just trying to draft a quick text to Chloe about my direct deposit that hasn't hit yet (it's been four days ugh). I know it's only $85 but I'm mildly spiraling like what if she's lowkey punishing me because I submitted the wrong voided check form at first??? Which is probably insane lol but still. Anyway I want something super breezy and friendly, like zero confrontational energy. Can you help me write two sentences to send her?

Hey Chloe! Just checking in since my direct deposit hasn’t come through yet—do you know when I should expect it? Let me know if you need anything else from me to get it sorted, and thanks for your help!

Okay but like... what if she's literally just stalling because I sent the wrong form first?? I know that's crazy lol but the timing is suspicious. Anyway, can you make that draft slightly warmer? Like add a "no rush" or something?

The timing alone doesn’t mean she’s stalling—an admin delay is a plausible explanation, especially with a corrected form. You can keep it warm without apologizing for checking on your pay:

“Hey Chloe, hope you’re having a good week! No rush on replying, but I wanted to check when my direct deposit might come through and whether you need anything else from me—thanks so much for your help!”

Okay okay that's fair lol. You're probably right I'm just being paranoid. The draft looks good! One tiny tweak though — can you take out the "hope you're having a good week" part? It feels a little corporate for a text 😅
Hey Chloe! No rush on replying, but I wanted to check when my direct deposit might come through and whether you need anything else from me—thanks so much for your help!
Okay I think I'll send it now lol. But real talk — if she replies with something vague like "working on it" should I just let it go or ask again in a few days??

Yep—if she says “working on it,” you can thank her **and ask for a rough timeline**:

“Thanks for checking on it! Do you have a rough idea of when it might come through?”

If she can’t give you a date, following up in a couple of business days is reasonable. If she gives you a date, wait until then. You don’t have to let it go indefinitely—$85 is still your money, and a friendly follow-up isn’t confrontational.
Okay you're right, $85 is still my money lol. Okay I'll send it! But now I'm second-guessing — should I send it now at 9pm on a Friday or wait til Monday morning??

I’d wait until Monday morning—this isn’t urgent tonight, and it’s more likely to get seen during work hours. Your “no rush” wording is friendly, but you don’t need to make yourself available all weekend either 😅 Save the draft, and let yourself clock out from this one until Monday.
